 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 90,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 10.02.2012 at about 3.00 p.m, when the Petitioner was travelling in an Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP02Y1136 with his grand mother and others and when they reached Kadrepalli village, on Kadirepalli - Gundumala road,
Madakashira, Ananthapur District, at that time, the driver of the said Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP02Y1136 has driven the same in a rash and negligent manner and due to over speed, the auto was toppled.
Due to the said impact, the Petitioner was fell down and had sustained grievous head injuries and other parts of the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Hindupur and after first aid, he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
He had spent Rs.15,00,000/ towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment charges.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was doing Tution and was earning of Rs.8,000/ per month.
The accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP02Y1136 by its driver.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending auto and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Written statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.2 in its Written statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2515/2019 sustained by the Narasimha Murthy vs Rajashekar.

N on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146211983/
2 Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further it contended that, the driver of the offending auto did not had a valid driving license to drive the auto at the time of the accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the rival Pleadings, my learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries due to RTA alleged to have been occurred on 10.02.2012 at about 2.00 p.m., near Kadrepalli village, on Kadirepalli - Gundumala road, Madakashira, Ananthapura district, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP02Y1136?
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?

7. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 20 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P20 and has examined 3 witnesses as PW.2 and to 4 and got marked 7 documents and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.R1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.

8. The learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied on the following decisions:
1. ILR 2000 KAR 1803, between B.H. Rangaiah Vs H.R.V. Basavaraju and another SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2515/2019 9.

sentences.text:
Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative. Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order, for the following :
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP02Y1136 by its driver.
Narasimha Murthy vs Rajashekar.

N on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146211983/
3 11.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP02Y1136 by its driver.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 20 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P20 and he has reiterated the Petition averments in his Chief affidavit.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P5 are the True copies of Charge sheet, FIR, Complaint, Wound certificate,
Charge sheet and Discharge summary.

Ex.P6 to 20 are the Aadhaar card, Prescriptions, Medical bills, Discharge summary, Prescriptions, Inpatient records, OPD book, Photos and CD, Discharge summary, Diagnostic Center Report, Prescriptions and Medical bills.

13. Upon going through the Ex.P1 and 2 and Ex.P2(a) i.e., FIR and Complaint shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Boya Polamma W/o Chinna Bommaiah, before Madakasira Police Station,
the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP02Y1136 for the offences punishable under sec.337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2515/2019 which shows that the Petitioner had sustained the grievous injuries.

Ex.P4 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Madakasira Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending auto for the offences punishable under Sec.337 of IPC.
14.

Ex.P6 to 20 are the Aadhaar card, Prescriptions, Medical bills, Discharge summary,
Prescriptions, Inpatient records, OPD book, Photos and CD, Discharge summary, Diagnostic Center Report, Prescriptions and Medical bills.
P.W.1 is subjected for crossexamination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.

PW.2 to PW.4 are the Medical Record Technicians by name Nagaraju, Raghu Y.C and Sudesh and they got marked 7 documents at Ex.P21 to 27 and they deposed that they does not know the contents of the documents which they produced before the Court.
To rebut the SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2515/2019 evidence of Petitioner, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.R1 and 2.
In the crossexamination, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the version of the Petitioner.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending auto bearing Reg.No.KA03AH7053 by its driver and in the said accident, he had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No. 2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending auto by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 26 years.

Further, in the Aadhaar card i.e.,
Ex.P6, the birth year of the Petitioner was shown as 1993.
The accident took SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2515/2019 place on 10.02.2012.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 19 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
Narasimha Murthy vs Rajashekar.

4 17.

Upon going through the medical records i.e., Ex.P3 Wound Certificate shows the injury i.e.,
Laceration upper end of occipital region of size 0.5cm X  cm horizontally bleeding.
Ex.P5 is the Discharge summary of Victoria hospital pertaining to the Petitioner which shows that the date of admission was 11.02.2012 and Discharge date was 15.02.2012.
The date of accident was 10.02.2012.
So, Ex.5 shows the Diagnosis is for Blunt Trauma Abdomen.
The treatment was taken in the said hospital immediately on the next date of accident.
Hence, though Ex.P3 Wound certificate does not shows the pain or injury to the abdomen, the very next day, he has undergone for the treatment of abdomen.
Further, Ex.P7 is the Prescriptions form for Lab investigation dated 19.11.2012 for clinical examination of the Petitioner in the Institute of Nephro Urology.

SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2515/2019 Ex.P9 is the Discharge summary of Institute of Nephro Urology shows the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 15.05.2012 to 22.05.2012 and the date of surgery was conducted on 18.05.2012.
The History shows "blunt injury abdomen on 11.02.2012 and on that admission P/u catheterisation done."
Ex . P10 - Discharge summary of Teja Nursing Home shows the Petitioner was admitted from 03.03.2021 to 12.03.2021 as an inpatient for Long Segment Structure.
Ex.P12 is also the report of Nephro Urology about the treatment taken by the Petitioner.

Ex.P13 is the OPD book of the Victoria hospital relating to the Petitioner about the treatment taken on 18.02.2012 and the same also shows the alleged H/o blunt trauma to the abdomen about 9 days back.
Ex.P14 & 15 are Photos and CD.

Ex.P16 is the Discharge summary of the Fortis hospital which shows the date of admission on 08.08.2022 and date of discharge on 12.08.2022 and the Chief Complaint is the "Petitioner Mr. Narashimha SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2515/2019 Murthy presented with history of RTA, not able to pass urine per urethrally S/P progressive perineal urethroplasty on 03.03.2022."

So, the Complaint and the diagnosis made to the Petitioner at the time of accident and the recent documents i.e., Ex.P16 corroborates about the blunt trauma to the abdomen and the treatment taken for the same.
18.
The Petitioner did not choose to examine the doctor who has issued the Wound Certificate as per Ex.P3.
The Petitioner has produced the Medical bills to prove expenditure towards medicines.
The bills at Ex.P8& 20 would reveal that the Petitioner had spent Rs.54,950/ towards medicines.

19. However, PW.1 has not examined any doctor and in the absence of physical disability and considering the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the medical expenses incurred for the treatment and other expenses, this Tribunal is SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2515/2019 of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.1,25,000/ would be just and proper.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.1,25,000/ with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realisation.

20. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP02Y1136.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Though, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Administrative Officer by name Himendra Kartantik Simha M.N as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.R1 and Narasimha Murthy vs Rajashekar.

N on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146211983/
5 2
and taken contention that the Policy does not cover the risk of the passenger of the offending vehicle and he has not proved the same with cogent evidence.

The Court has taken SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2515/2019 Judicial Notice about the document produced by the Petitioner i.e., the Information provided by the National Insurance Company under RTI which shows the Policy covering the risk of 3 passengers and driver/owner of the vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
21. Issue No. 3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2 , I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for Global  Compensation of Rs.1,25,000/ along with  SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2515/2019 interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the Offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the amount is meager, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
